A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FARM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Corresponding material can be matched across renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MoleculeNet results in Tables 2–3, masking and component ablations, and analyses of learned representations.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds ToxCast evaluation, a BRICS comparison, vocabulary-growth analysis, and quantum-property predictions.

M1.justification: The FG tokenization, BERT encoder, ComplEx embeddings, GCN link prediction, and contrastive objectives are retained. Larger-group-first detection and property discretization are newly documented, but the PDFs do not establish an underlying procedure change.

E1.justification: v3 adds ToxCast, covering 617 toxicity endpoints and 8,575 molecules, and a separate quantum-property dataset with 25 prediction targets in Appendix E. These substantially extend evaluation coverage beyond the retained twelve MoleculeNet datasets. The documented pretraining sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: BRICS becomes an evaluated fragmentation comparator across six tasks in v3 Table 4; v1 only discusses it as prior work. Existing benchmark and component-ablation comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include R² evaluation for quantum properties and a corpus-size vocabulary sweep. Existing MoleculeNet metrics and split policies remain. Appendix G reports 20 BERT epochs on an A100, while retained Appendix D.1 specifies 15 epochs on two V100s; their relationship is unexplained and does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive tests of fragmentation choice against BRICS across six tasks and of vocabulary growth, saturation, and coverage as corpus size increases. Existing masking sensitivity, component ablations, attention analysis, and embedding analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 9 specifies standard deviations over ten runs for the new quantum-property evaluation. The existing MoleculeNet practice of reporting means and standard deviations across three seeds remains unchanged.

E6.justification: New results include FARM's ToxCast ROC-AUC of 69.9±0.5, six-task BRICS comparisons, 25 quantum-property R² scores ranging from 0.755 to 0.995, and vocabulary-growth and coverage measurements. Shared benchmark, masking, and component-ablation values remain unchanged; these additions do not represent improvements on the original evaluations.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, ComplEx formulation, graph-convolution update, and link-prediction equations are retained. Equation renumbering and abbreviated cosine-similarity notation do not change their substance; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The headline state-of-the-art claim expands from 10 of 12 to 11 of 13 MoleculeNet tasks, and transfer-learning performance becomes an explicit contribution. The principal tokenization, structural-learning, and representation-integration contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 removes the stated rare fused-ring/OOV limitation while retaining the absence of full 3D representations. It interprets new vocabulary measurements as evidence of saturation and high coverage, and attributes BRICS' weaker performance to larger fragments and rare-token vocabularies.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, overlapping-group detection priority, and integer discretization of continuous knowledge-graph properties. Appendix G newly documents approximately 100 million parameters, training time, and hardware specifications. Most existing implementation recipes are retained.

R1.justification: v3 emphasizes chemically defined functional groups over general motifs or mined subgraphs and condenses the BRICS/RDKit discussion. It adds Angello et al. (2024) for the quantum-property dataset and removes Radford (2018) and Xu et al. (2018); most cited works remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around concrete token examples and complementary sequence/graph representations. Related work is condensed, ablations receive main-text summaries, and the appendices are reorganized into separate evaluation, ablation, and computational-resource sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, the salicylic-acid/aspirin figure is removed, and retained figures are reformatted or relocated. v3 adds BRICS and quantum-property tables and a ToxCast column. Document-wide typography, headers, table sizing, and figure placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new BRICS comparison directly tests a central design choice that v1 supported less directly. Vocabulary analysis, clearer tokenization explanations, broader evaluation, and a code-access link also help. These gains are limited by missing split and sample details for the quantum-property evaluation, ambiguous corpus-size descriptions, and unreconciled training-resource accounts.
